Photograph: UKRAINIAN PRESIDENTIAL PRESS SERVICE/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Volodymyr Zelenskyy makes a presentation to a Ukrainian soldier during a visit to frontline positions where he named two of Ukraine’s most prominent commanders to spearhead defence of Ukraine’s ‘fortress belt’. Photograph: UKRAINIAN PRESIDENTIAL PRESS SERVICE/AFP/Getty Images Russia-Ukraine war at a glance Ukraine Explainer Ukraine war briefing: Reboot of ‘fortress belt’ defences as Zelenskyy visits frontline Two modern commanders appointed on Donetsk front after dismissal of ‘Soviet-era’ Oleksandr Syrskyi as head of military. What we know on day 1,645 Warren Murray and agencies Wed 26 Aug 2026 21.34 EDT Last modified on Wed 26 Aug 2026 21.35 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Volodymyr Zelenskyy has appointed two of Ukraine’s most prominent commanders to oversee and strengthen defences of the “fortress belt” of industrialised cities in the Donetsk region . Visiting the frontline, Zelenskyy said Third Army Corps leader Andrii Biletskyi and Denys Prokopenko, commander of the First Corps ⁠Azov, would head new groupings. Both units are known for embracing Nato-style doctrine and new technology. Russian forces are putting pressure on the cities of Kostiantynivka, Kramatorsk and Sloviansk – all critical strongholds for Ukraine. According to open-source mapping group Deep State, Moscow’s ‌troops have been infiltrating deeper into Kostiantynivka, with the Ukrainians weeding them out from houses, basements and ruins. Russia was also stepping up its air and artillery ​attacks on Kramatorsk and Sloviansk to prepare for a targeted offensive on those cities, Deep State said. Ukrainian military analyst Mykola Bielieskov told Reuters the appointments were “the right move” in giving Ukraine’s new commander in chief, Mykhailo Drapatyi, greater scope for strategic planning . His predecessor, the “Soviet-era” general Oleksandr Syrskyi, was criticised for micromanagement. Ukrainian drone forces commander Robert Brovdi, a leader of Kyiv’s mid and long-range strike campaigns, praised the appointments as an important step towards “network-centric warfare … This is exactly what ‘Smart War’ is,” he posted. Ukraine hit ⁠16 sites in Russia ⁠over ⁠the past day ​including oil facilities and ⁠logistics , Zelenskyy said ⁠on Wednesday. The ‌targets also included ‌airfields, a missile unit, a military enterprise and infrastructure that ‌Moscow uses to launch attacks against ​Ukraine. Ukraine’s military general staff said its forces struck a Lukoil refinery overnight in Kstovo, in Russia’s Nizhny Novgorod region, setting it on fire. The refinery can process 125m barrels annually. Long-range Ukrainian drones burned a Wildberries warehouse to the ground in the Tambov region south-east of Moscow, Russian authorities said on Wednesday. A ⁠ Russian guided aerial ⁠bomb ⁠attack seriously ​damaged a combined ⁠heat and power plant ⁠in ​ Ukraine’s southern ‌city ‌of Kherson , ‌the plant’s owner, Ukrainian energy company Naftogaz, said ‌on Wednesday. The extent of ​the damage would be ⁠assessed as ​soon as ​the security ​situation allowed, ​Naftogaz ‌said. There were explosions ​in ⁠the ⁠Ukrainian capital ​of ‌Kyiv ‌early ‌on Thursday, ‌a ​Reuters ⁠witness ​said. Around the same time, Russia ⁠attacked an industrial facility ⁠in ⁠the central ​Ukrainian city of ⁠Kryvyi Rih with ballistic missiles, ⁠injuring two ​people, ‌said Oleksandr ‌Vilkul, the head of ‌the city’s defence council. It came after Bloomberg reported that Russia was considering ⁠stepping up its ballistic missile strikes ⁠on ⁠Kyiv , including ​targets in the city centre, ⁠and on critical infrastructure elsewhere in ⁠Ukraine after concluding that ​efforts ‌to negotiate ‌a peace deal ‌had reached a dead end. While Ukraine has repeatedly offered ceasefires and negotiations, the Kremlin has not altered its demands – chief among which is total control of Ukraine’s Donbas region. Volodymyr Zelenskyy has awarded Ukraine’s Order of Freedom to Elon Musk , whose SpaceX has provided Starlink satellite internet to Ukraine’s military. Musk has restricted its use over Russian territory – a policy Zelenskyy hopes to change so that Ukrainian weapons can use Starlink to navigate to their targets. Ukraine freed 10 Russian prisoners of war , Russia’s human rights commissioner said on Wednesday. On Monday, Russia released 10 Ukrainian prisoners of war who were previously thought to be missing. A pro-Russian hacker group on Wednesday claimed responsibility for a cyber-attack on Digdir, the Norwegian government’s digital services agency. The denial-of-service (DDOS) attacks tried to overwhelm the agency’s computers to block services, including one that enables citizens to use one login across multiple public services. A Digdir spokesperson said the agency still managed to keep the services running “practically all the time”. The pro-Russian hacker group Server Killers said it attacked because Norway renewed its security cooperation with Ukraine on 23 August. https://www.nme.com/news/music/watch-cha.text: Chase & Status at the 2026 Leeds Festival at Bramham Park on August 28, 2026 in Leeds, England. (Photo by Matthew Baker/Getty Images) Chase & Status brought Reading 2026 to a close with a star-studded headline set – check out footage below. The UK production duo were the final act on the festival’s main stage – now known as The Grid – at Little John’s Farm last night (August 30), following on from co-headliner Florence + The Machine . Advertisement They were joined by ArrDee for ‘Liquor & Cigarettes’, NADIAH for ‘Count On Me’, D Double E for ‘Levels’ and Novelist for ‘NRG’ in the first half of their set, which took place against a torrential downpour for the Reading crowd. IRAH contributed vocals during a mash-up of the duo’s remixes of Britney Spears ‘ ‘Toxic’ and Shy FX and UK Apache’s ‘Original Nuttah’, while Flowdan came out for ‘Baddadan’ and Takura joined for ‘No Problem’. WATCH Tom Grennan made an appearance on ‘All Goes Wrong’, Clementine Douglas was there for ‘Mixed Emotions’, Debbie sang on ‘Gone Too Far’, and Liam Bailey came out for the band’s classic single ‘Blind Faith’. “If you’ve been with us since the beginning…old and new fans, we appreciate the fuck out of you. Reading, make some fucking noise for yourselves,” the duo said as the show came to an end. UK viewers can watch the full set here . Chase & Status’ Reading 2026 setlist was: ‘Rage’ ‘Selecta’ ‘Streetlife’ ‘Disgruntled’ ‘Liquor & Cigarettes’ (with ArrDee) ‘Count On Me’ (with NADIAH) ‘Levels’ (with D Double E) ‘Don’t Be Scared’ ‘NRG’ (with Novelist) ‘Toxic (Chase & Status Remix)’ / ‘Original Nuttah 25 (Chase & Status Remix)’ (with IRAH) ‘Baddadan’ (with Flowdan) ‘Disconnect’ ‘No Problem’ (with Takura) ‘Backbone’ ‘Mixed Emotions’ (with Clementine Douglas) ‘Gone Too Far’ (with Debbie) ‘All Goes Wrong’ (with Tom Grennan) ‘Carnage’ ‘Blind Faith’ (with Liam Bailey) ‘Program’ (with IRAH) Recommended Earlier this month, the duo joined Skrillex during his own headline set at Boomtown for a surprise B2B performance. They played an unreleased track with Brazilian vocals, with many fans speculating that it points to an upcoming collaboration between the two. They also performed at Romania’s Electric Castle festival in July, where their rendition of ‘Baddadan’ sparked “pandemonium among hordes of skanking teens” . The duo are currently preparing to release their eighth studio album, ‘Generic Everything’, on October 9. The record includes Reading setlist tracks ‘Disgruntled’, ‘Levels’, ‘Gone Too Far’ and ‘Carnage’. https://www.politico.eu/article/palantir.text: LONDON — The Mayor of London Sadiq Khan and U.S. tech company Palantir have agreed to drop legal proceedings relating to a blocked £50 million police contract. Palantir brought a claim against the Mayor’s Office for Policing and Crime in the High Court in June after Khan’s deputy mayor refused to sign off on the £50 million contract with the Metropolitan Police for the provision of an AI and data analysis service. In July, lawyers working on behalf of MOPAC in turn accused the Met Police and Palantir of coordinating to fix the outcome of the procurement process in breach of the rules . Palantir claimed Khan’s office had unlawfully blocked the contract over the company's “values and ethics,” based on media reporting. Advertisement Advertisement A full trial was expected in January but on Wednesday both sides agreed to “settle their differences” and drop the allegations without admitting liability. They will each cover their own legal costs. In an agreed statement , the two sides said MOPAC’s decision to block the Palantir contract was “not based on Palantir’s values or ethics or any wider reporting about the company,” though MOPAC said it “recognizes Palantir’s concerns that media reporting of a statement from the Mayor's spokesperson before the decision was taken could have incorrectly created the impression that an assessment of the company’s values had been a factor in that decision.” “MOPAC’s consideration was based upon its statutory role of examining spend proposals, against the appropriate legal tests and the relevant guidance on procurement, governance, affordability and ensuring value for money for Londoners and in doing so it focussed on the available information at the time,” the statement said. The settlement also notes that MOPAC is working with Metropolitan Police Service to re-run a competitive procurement for the relevant service, which Palantir will be eligible to bid for. “MOPAC does not have, and has never had, any policy of not contracting with Palantir,” the statement confirms, while noting the mayor’s duty is to ensure “all procurements are lawful, fair, transparent and deliver value for money.” “London is the technology capital of Europe, and I am proud that leading software firms choose the city as their home. Palantir makes a significant contribution to jobs and investment in the capital, employing a large number of Londoners whose services have been procured legally by organizations across the U.K. and beyond,” Khan said. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/videos/c65yng.text: Why Zelensky's meeting with Burnham matters Why Zelensky's meeting with Burnham matters Close Prime Minister Andy Burnham welcomed President Volodymyr Zelensky to Downing Street on Wednesday, as the Ukrainian leader looks to shore up his European allies five years into Russia's war on Ukraine. Burnham told Zelensky that Britain "would forever stand by you" and that he was accelerating the delivery of air defences to Ukraine. Burnham previously told MPs that he would try to "repair bridges" between Ukraine and the United States and that Ukraine won't leave "empty-handed". The two leaders met at No 10 Downing Street where Zelensky was welcomed with a military ceremonial guard - thought to be a first for a foreign leader. BBC World News correspondent Joe Inwood explains what we know about the meeting. Read more about the meeting in London. https://www.dw.com/en/italy-students-and.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OrcS Prefer DW on Google Students demanding education and housing support joined workers protesting rising living costs and military spending across Italy Image: Andreas Solaro/AFP Advertisement Tens of thousands of students and workers marched across Italy on Friday, demanding more education funding and relief from rising living costs. The rallies followed weeks of student tent camps and school occupations, with a general strike bringing workers into the streets alongside them. Demonstrations took place in dozens of cities, including Rome, Milan, Turin, Bologna, Genoa and Naples. Police were deployed in large numbers after earlier protests descended into rioting. Why were students and workers protesting? Demonstrators criticized Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni 's right-wing government over low wages, rising fuel prices and military spending. Students demanded more money for schools and universities. In Rome, university student Beatrice Chilelli said students were "at a breaking point." "They can't afford to pay exorbitant tuition fees, and rent... which weighs heavily on their parents' shoulders," the 21-year-old told AFP. Like their French counterparts, students in Italy have been protesting for weeks Image: Marco Bertorello/AFP The USB trade union called a general strike, with truck drivers, taxi drivers and farmers among those joining the protests. Disruption to public transport remained limited on Friday morning. Thousands marched from Rome's Termini station past the Colosseum, accompanied by two tractors and a taxi. "We need more houses, not bombs!" one group chanted. Did the protests turn violent? Minor scuffles broke out between demonstrators and riot police in Turin at the start of the march. No major clashes had been reported by midday. In Milan, the procession headed away from the city center, where rioters looted shops, damaged property and clashed with police after a cost-of-living demonstration two weeks earlier. Authorities also increased protection around landmarks, including Rome's Colosseum and Milan's cathedral. The student protests have drawn momentum from similar movements in France and Spain . Teachers, retirees and other workers also joined Friday's rallies.
